page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with marginal notes in the right margin. Running head at the top, page number above it, catchword and gathering signature at the foot.

main_text.p: Sunt & alia pemmatum apud veteres ge- nera, quæ liba appellarunt, ac ex cafeo, fa- rina filiginea aut tritica, ouisque fiebant, quidam addunt crocum lactisque pinguedi- nem.
Huius generis eft itrion dictum, cu- jus sæpe mentionem facit Galenus & a- lii, componiturque ex sesamo & mel- le, hodie loco sesami fumunt amygda- las.Itrion.

Eft Tracta, mixtura quædam ex fermento & farina compacta, manibus sæpius in for- mam longam planamque tracta, vnde et- iam nomen emanauit. Itali Tiratas à tra- hendo nominant, si subigitur vuæ passæ fuc- co melior fit & suauior.Tracta.
Infitiaetiam huc referre licet, siue inficia, quæ fiebant ex variis carnibus tritis pi- pereque commixtis, vel etiam ex pi- scibus diuersis, teste Alexandro Tralli- ano.Infitia.
Simile huic edulium tetrapharmacum eft Adriano Imperat. carum, quod ex phasiano, sumine, perna, & cruftulo compofitum fuit- se, narrat Spartanus.Edulium Hadriani Imp.
Qui primò Itria, Tractam, & id genus liba in mensis ponunt, illaudandi sunt: nam cer- tum est eiusmodi panificiorum genera nullo tanda.Itria in cibis vi-

page.notes: The running head is set with spaced capitals and read as PROROGANDA; the page number reads 251 but the final digit is uncertain. "pemmatum", "Itrion" and "Tanda" are doubtful readings in an old, faded print. The right-margin notes are partly cut off and their wording is uncertain. The catchword "fermen-" and signature "P 4" are read from the foot of the page.
